title: Escape-seq & Unicode cleanse - pocket notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for handling literal escape sequences, invisible unicode, and emoji/variation selector cases when we prepare text for labeling. Aim is to reduce annotator confusion and maintain provenance so we can revert if needed.

High-level decisions (working):
- Keep visual fidelity for human annotators; prefer presentation-friendly transforms rather than aggressive stripping.
- Apply Unicode canonical normalization (NFC) by default so composed glyphs stay consistent across sources.
- Convert JSON/CSV-style escaped sequences to their intended characters only when the source semantics indicate the escape encodes a real control character (e.g., "\\n" in a JSON payload that should be a newline). If ambiguous, preserve literal escape and flag for review.
- Strip zero-width and bidi control characters only when they are clearly injected noise (heuristic below). Record removed chars in a remediation log field.

Quick heuristics:
- If source_type == "json_string" or filename ends with .json and the field looks like escaped text (contains "\\n" or "\\t"), attempt JSON unescape and re-run tokenization. But keep original as metadata_orig_text.
- If text contains high ratio (>5%) of variation selectors (VS-16 etc) or ZERO-WIDTH chars, mark as "weird-unicode" and surface to annotator with small note: "invisible chars removed for display; underlying text preserved".
- For emoji sequences, preserve ZWJ-joined sequences intact as one token for entity spans unless label spans are explicitly character-level.
- For combining marks (diacritics): normalize to NFC; do not decompose (NFD) unless downstream matching requires codepoint-level alignment.

Examples (input -> what annotator sees -> recommended action):
1) Raw: "Hello\\nWorld"
   - If field is JSON string: unescape -> "Hello\nWorld" (two-line text) -> annotate normally; store orig_text = "Hello\\nWorld"
   - If plain user text (someone literally typed backslash-n): preserve literal "\\n"; add question flag: literal-escape?

2) Raw: "Mr. O\u2019Brien" (unicode escape for right single quote)
   - Unescape -> "Mr. O’Brien"; normalize NFC -> display "Mr. O’Brien"
   - Tags: NAME; do not split on apostrophe.

3) Raw: "userid: 1234" (embedded NULL)
   - Heuristic: binary control chars (except common whitespace) -> strip and record positions; flag for adjudication if control char breaks token boundaries that could change labels.

4) Raw: "p\n" (CRLF escaped weirdness in scraped HTML)
   - Normalize newlines to \n, but preserve paragraph boundaries for labeling multi-line addresses.

5) Raw: "apple\uFE0F" vs "apple" (emoji variation selector)
   - Treat both as same logical token for entity labels, but store variation in provenance metadata.

Label-span guidance (edgecases):
- When invisible characters sit inside an entity span (e.g., zero-width joiner inside a long product SKU), include them in the span if removing them would change the visual token. If they are clearly injected (tens of ZW chars), trim and annotate with comment on original content.
- When a label boundary falls adjacent to an escape sequence that resolves into whitespace ("\\n", "\\t"), do adjudication: prefer label that matches visual contiguous token on display after unescape.
- For language-specific punctuation (e.g., Arabic punctuation + bidi markers), prefer to normalize but add a note: "bidi normalized" so downstream QA knows we altered presentation.

Adjudication questions to include in UI when flagged:
- Did we correctly interpret escaped sequences as real control characters?
- Did removing invisible unicode change label semantics (e.g., merged tokens that should be separate)?
- Should emoji sequences be split or treated as part of surrounding text for this label type?

Small regex cookbook (for pre-label cleaning):
- JSON-unescape candidate: detect "\\\\[btnfr\\\\]" or "\\\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}" patterns; sample 100 docs and confirm before bulk unescape.
- Zero-width probe: /[\u200B-\u200F\uFEFF]/g -> count and record positions.
- Bidi controls: /[\u202A-\u202E]/g -> flag for review.

QA / sampling suggestions:
- For any automatic change, keep original text in metadata_orig_text and add a difflog entry: "removed ZWSP at pos 12" so we can audit regressions.
- Build a small evaluation set (n=200) with common patterns: escaped JSON strings, ZWSP injected, emoji ZWJ sequences, combining marks. Use to measure annotator disagreement pre/post-normalization.

Implementation notes for pipeline engineers:
- Add a boolean field cleaned_escape_unescaped = true/false in the prelabel payload. Default false until we have sample approval.
- Store both normalized_text and display_text. normalized_text = NFC + unescaped + control-removed (for model training only). display_text = what annotator sees (NFC + selective unescape).
- Provide a fast toggle in annotation UI: "Show original raw" so annotators can open the original string with hex codes when uncertain.

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-up):
- Which label types (NER PERSON/ORG/PRODUCT/ADDRESS) are sensitive to removal of ZW chars? Need to run small experiment.
- Agree whether to canonicalize emoji variants for embeddings downstream (lossy) or keep as-is and rely on tokenization layer.
- Edge-case policy for malicious bidi/ZW injection (likely security): route to SRE/security if repeated in web-scraped content.

Notes to self and quick links:
- See DL ticket: DL-1123 for initial sampling results.
- Conversation in Slack thread (Dec 11) with @Evan about whether to aggressively unescape CSV fields.
- Confluence draft page linked above contains longer rationale and sample code snippets (Python ICU/ftfy examples).

If you use this doc: copy to a team-owned note and update the TODOs checklist. Keep the original raw text in all outputs until we have a final policy.

-- Sofia
  (short-lived pocket reference; not authoritative until we lock in rules)
